name: rowSdDiffs
title: Standard deviation of sequential differences for each row

origin.description: Estimation of scale based on sequential-order differences, corresponding to the scale estimates provided by stats::var, stats::sd, stats::mad and stats::IQR.
origin.usage:
rowSdDiffs(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, diff = 1L,
  trim = 0, ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length N or a numeric N by K matrix.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: diff
arguments.text: The positional distance of elements for which the difference should be calculated.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: A double in [0, 1/2] specifying the fraction of observations to be trimmed from each end of the sorted values before estimation.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: n-order difference MAD estimates, like stats::mad, apply a consistency factor for the Gaussian standard deviation. The IQR estimates do not. That factor would be 1 / (2 * qnorm(3/4)) and has to be applied by hand. Differences are computed by diff2, which is a faster diff. The result is then divided by 2^diff for the variance and by sqrt(2)^diff otherwise. The divisor uses the original diff, while diff2 truncates the order with as.integer.
origin.value: A numeric vector with one value per row.

translation.description: Estimation of scale based on sequential-order differences, corresponding to the scale estimates provided by stats::var, stats::sd, stats::mad and stats::IQR.
translation.usage:
rowSdDiffs(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, diff=1,
  trim=0, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K numeric array. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns. A one-dimensional vector is filled by matrix() in R and here must already be two-dimensional; pass a column-major reshape when reproducing matrix(data, nrow).

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to include. None uses every row. Subsetting follows base R: zero is dropped, negatives exclude, and a missing row index inserts a missing row.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to include. None uses every column. The same base-R rules as rows apply, and the differences follow the selected column order.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are dropped before the differences are formed. This is na.rm in R. The default is False.

arguments.name: diff
arguments.text: Order of difference passed to diff2, default 1. diff2 truncates a non-integer with as.integer. The scale correction still uses this original value, so 1.9 is a first difference divided by 2^1.9. Zero skips the difference. A negative value is an error.

arguments.name: trim
arguments.text: Fraction trimmed from each end of the sorted differences before the scale estimate. The default is 0. The kept slice is lo:hi with lo = floor(n * trim) + 1 and hi = n + 1 - lo. A missing value in that slice makes the estimate missing when trim is positive.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: This is useNames in R. TRUE or FALSE is accepted. The result is always a plain array; names are not attached.

translation.details: The same estimate is applied to each row after an optional base-R subset of rows and columns. Differences come from matrixstats.diff2.diff2, with lag 1. The estimate is the sample standard deviation stats::sd, divided by sqrt(2)^diff. stats::var is the compensated two-pass sample variance. stats::sd is its square root. stats::mad is constant times the median absolute deviation from the median, default constant 1.4826. The quartiles follow stats::quantile, default type 7. Extra arguments are accepted and ignored, as in R. Integer input is read as float64, and R's integer NA becomes a missing value before diff2.
translation.value: A one-dimensional float64 array with one value per row.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.vardiff import rowSdDiffs

rowSdDiffs(np.array([1, 5, 2, 8, 4, 1, 9, 3, 2, 6, 4, 7], dtype=float).reshape((4, 3), order="F"))
